TITLE: [YSQL] Memory accumulated across preloading CatCache during start-up
RELEASE NOTE: Reduce memory usage during start-up by avoiding accumulation from repeated sys-scans on catalog preloads.
DETAILS: Limit memory consumption during start-up by preventing accumulation of memory from multiple sys-scans performed on catalog preloads in CatCache. This change avoids high memory usage that previously occurred due to holding memory throughout the preload process, reducing the likelihood of out-of-memory errors on smaller instances.

TITLE: Automated detection, attribution, and reporting of test failures in scheduled integration builds
RELEASE NOTE: Automate classification and attribution of test failures in scheduled integration builds to streamline triage and reporting.
DETAILS: Automate detection, classification, and attribution of test failures in scheduled integration builds that cover batches of commits. Automatically distinguish failures as known bugs, known flakes, or new issues requiring investigation, eliminating manual scanning. Attribute new failures to the precise commit responsible by comparing failure rates before and after the suspect change. Group multiple related failures into a single report assigned to the commit author or area owner, providing failure headlines, failure rates with sample counts, rerun commands, and log excerpts for effective debugging without reruns.

TITLE: Automated detection, attribution, and reporting of test failures in scheduled integration builds
RELEASE NOTE: Automate classification and attribution of test failures in scheduled integration builds to streamline triage and reporting.
DETAILS: Automate detection, classification, and attribution of test failures in scheduled integration builds that cover batches of commits. Automatically distinguish failures as known bugs, known flakes, or new issues requiring investigation, eliminating manual scanning. Attribute new failures to the precise commit responsible by comparing failure rates before and after the suspect change. Group multiple related failures into a single report assigned to the commit author or area owner, providing failure headlines, failure rates with sample counts, rerun commands, and log excerpts for effective debugging without reruns.

TITLE: [DocDB] Add a per-tablet metric for overdue WAL fsync
RELEASE NOTE: Add a per-tablet gauge metric log_wal_sync_overdue_ms to track overdue WAL fsyncs against interval_durable_wal_write_ms.
DETAILS: Introduce the tablet-level gauge metric 'log_wal_sync_overdue_ms' which measures in milliseconds how long the oldest unsynced WAL entry has exceeded 'interval_durable_wal_write_ms'. This metric is zero when there is no unsynced WAL, the overdue threshold is not surpassed, the interval is disabled, or when 'durable_wal_write=true'. It enables precise monitoring and alerting on WAL fsync delays that were previously untrackable, helping ensure timely WAL durability especially with 'durable_wal_write=false'. Aggregating this metric across tablets allows detection of tablets not meeting fsync timing guarantees.

TITLE: [YSQL] `TestYbAsh#testPreparedStatements` fails on master: Expected N to be greater than N |...
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent testPreparedStatements from failing sporadically by stabilizing prepared statement execution.
DETAILS: Reduce flakiness in the testPreparedStatements unit test by addressing the root cause of intermittent failures where expected values were not correctly compared. This change improves test reliability by ensuring consistent preparation and execution of statements in YSQL, particularly on the arm-alma8-clang21-release build lane. It eliminates the previous 12% failure rate and prevents regression, maintaining stable validation for prepared statements in regular test runs.

TITLE: [YSQL] Relcache preload keeps every decoded catalog row until the whole relcache is built
RELEASE NOTE: Reduce memory usage during full catalog preload by freeing decoded catalog rows promptly after use.
DETAILS: Reduce the peak memory consumption during full catalog preload by deallocating decoded catalog rows immediately after processing each relation, instead of retaining all decoded rows until the preload completes. This eliminates unnecessary retention of data from pg_class, pg_attribute, pg_attrdef, pg_constraint, pg_trigger, pg_policy, pg_partitioned_table, and pg_index scans in the UpdateRelationCacheContext, which previously caused significant transient memory usage spikes during backend startup, especially with large schemas and when ysql_catalog_preload_additional_tables=true.

TITLE: [DocDB] `QLStressTest.ShortTimeLeaderDoesNotReplicateNoOp` fails on master: Runtime error Step down failed: error {...
RELEASE NOTE: Reduce failure rate of QLStressTest.ShortTimeLeaderDoesNotReplicateNoOp by stabilizing leader step down behavior.
DETAILS: Increase stability of leader step down during short term leader tests to lower failure incidences of QLStressTest.ShortTimeLeaderDoesNotReplicateNoOp. This targets reducing runtime errors related to leader step down failing, which previously caused test failures up to 28% recently. Stabilizing leader transitions improves test reliability and reduces flaky test runs in the master branch on arm-alma8-clang21-release lane.

TITLE: [DocDB] Master fails to load the sys catalog when the sys catalog tablet lists a table id twice
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent master leader exit during sys catalog load by handling duplicate YSQL system table IDs gracefully.
DETAILS: Avoid master leader exit when the sys catalog tablet's SysTabletsEntryPB.table_ids contains duplicate YSQL system table IDs by ensuring TabletLoader::Visit handles repeated IDs without triggering IllegalState errors. This change allows recovery from scenarios where a system table creation fails and retries leave stale IDs behind, preventing cluster leader loss and eliminating the need for manual sys catalog tablet entry edits or binary rollbacks. This fix addresses issues observed from versions 2024.2.0 onwards, improving stable master startup during sys catalog loading.

TITLE: [YSQL] Build 8abb6c5d on 2024.2: 2 lanes broken
RELEASE NOTE: Address build failures on arm-mac15-clang-release and mac15-clang-release by fixing compile and link errors.
DETAILS: Resolve compile and link errors causing build failures on arm-mac15-clang-release and mac15-clang-release lanes for the 2024.2 scheduled build at commit 8abb6c5d. This ensures successful completion of release builds on these configurations, enabling tests to run and maintain build stability across supported platforms.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#26813] DocDB: avoid tserver thread exhaustion
RELEASE NOTE: Limit remote bootstrap attempts to avoid tserver thread exhaustion by failing quickly when checkpoint lock is unavailable.
DETAILS: Prevent exhaustion of all tserver threads caused by repeated remote bootstrap attempts that stall on the checkpoint lock during disk I/O delays. By using a try_lock on the create_checkpoint_lock_ mutex, a thread unable to acquire the lock fails the RPC immediately instead of blocking. This enforces a maximum of two concurrent remote bootstrap threads per tablet, avoiding thread pile-up and improving system stability under rare slow bootstrap initiation conditions.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#30831] CDC: Align the WAL sort window for GetChanges across peers to prevent data loss
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent data loss in CDC by aligning WAL sort windows across peers during tablet leadership changes.
DETAILS: Prevent CDC data loss caused by out-of-order WAL records streamed during a tablet leadership change by aligning the WAL sort window for GetChanges across all tablet peers. This alignment ensures consistent handling of the wal_segment_index across replicas, preventing skipped records and ensuring all committed writes are streamed despite leadership transitions. This fix is critical when CDC lags and processes out-of-order apply operations spanning multiple WAL segments, guaranteeing replication continuity and accurate data consistency between source and sink systems.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#29457] YSQL: Fix testAvgWaitTime to work even when pool is null initially
RELEASE NOTE: Stabilize YSQL connection manager test by handling null pool stats and allowing zero wait time on initial check.
DETAILS: Improve stability of the YSQL connection manager test `TestStatsAndMetrics` by modifying it to handle scenarios where connection pool statistics are initially null. The test now treats the average wait time as zero if pool stats are not yet populated at the first metrics check, preventing false failures due to timing variations right after connection creation. Subsequent checks still assert that the pool metrics are populated, ensuring accurate metrics validation without flaky test behavior.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33375] docdb: fixed bloom use filter for queries on YCQL tables with STATIC columns
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent queries on YCQL tables with static columns from returning incomplete results by fixing bloom filter usage.
DETAILS: Avoid incomplete result sets or undercounted aggregates in YCQL queries on tables with static columns by correcting bloom filter classification during forward scans without hash key filters. This fix ensures that all relevant SST files are scanned correctly by disabling incorrect fixed-point bloom filter assumptions. The issue affected only SST-only queries without WHERE clauses filtering on hash keys or tokens, and YSQL is unaffected. To prevent partial results, add a partition_hash() condition on hash keys in the WHERE clause as a workaround if needed.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33348] docdb: Fix big shared memory segment id wrapping
RELEASE NOTE: Wrap big shared memory segment IDs at 2^22 to prevent mismatches and failures in large YSQL query responses.
DETAILS: Wrap big shared memory segment IDs around 2^22 to prevent ID truncation mismatch between TServer and PostgreSQL, which caused large YSQL queries to fail after 4,194,304 big-segment allocations. This fix ensures stable operation over long uptimes by avoiding permanent failures for large responses without needing a TServer restart. It stabilizes large query response handling, preventing silent ID overflows and eliminating staggered, node-specific failures in clusters due to ID counter wraparound issues.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33035,#33210] CDCSDK: harden GetChanges change metadata op handling
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent tserver crashes by safely handling change metadata ops for dropped colocated tables during GetChanges calls.
DETAILS: Avoid crashes by skipping change metadata operations referencing dropped colocated tables during GetChangesForCDCSDK processing. This ensures that when a colocated table has been dropped but earlier metadata operations remain in the WAL, the system no longer performs lookups that fail and cause tserver crashes. Handlers now log and skip such ops rather than crashing. This fix also addresses issues with schema-less change metadata ops by suppressing empty DDL records, preserving stream stability and preventing processing of outdated or invalid schema changes for dropped tables.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33393] CDC: Prevent VWAL memory spike due to a high start_lsn
RELEASE NOTE: Acknowledge filtered transactions with commit_lsn below start_lsn to prevent memory bloat in Virtual WAL during CDC.
DETAILS: Prevent memory bloat in Virtual WAL by acknowledging transactions filtered out by walsender when a large start_lsn is used in logical replication. Previously, transactions with commit_lsn less than start_lsn were filtered but never acknowledged, causing the Virtual WAL to retain metadata indefinitely and increasing memory usage. This change safely acknowledges these filtered transactions based on the start_lsn indicator that earlier data is no longer needed, enabling timely pruning of in-memory metadata and preventing memory spikes that could breach tserver memory limits.

TITLE: [#33479] DocDB: Do not GC a column tombstone that was not merged into its packed row
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent resurrecting deleted columns by skipping GC of unmerged column tombstones over packed rows during compaction.
DETAILS: Avoid resurrecting deleted column values during compaction by skipping garbage collection of column tombstones that have not been merged into their packed rows. When packed row compaction is disabled (e.g., with ysql_enable_packed_row=false), an unmerged tombstone would previously be dropped, causing the deleted column to reappear. Now, the system retains such tombstones until a compaction performs the merge. This behavior is controlled by the flag docdb_keep_unmerged_column_tombstones_over_packed_row (default true), allowing restoration of previous behavior if needed. This fix addresses permanent data inconsistencies caused by mixed compaction configurations across replicas.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32368] YSQL: Fix missed initialization of the PgClient::big_shared_memory_id_ field
RELEASE NOTE: Initialize and update big_shared_memory_ to correctly manage shared memory segments in PgClient.
DETAILS: Initialize the big_shared_memory_ field within PgClient to ensure proper tracking and management of large shared memory segments. Replace the previously unused and uninitialized fields big_shared_memory_id, big_shared_memory_object, and big_mapped_region with a single std::optional<BigSharedMemoryDescriptor> named big_shared_memory_. This change ensures that comparisons and operations on the shared memory segment are meaningful and accurate, preventing potential inconsistencies or errors related to shared memory handling in YSQL client interactions.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32180] YSQL: Fix money type overflow with SUM aggregate function
RELEASE NOTE: Throw "money out of range" error on MONEY type sum overflow instead of returning incorrect results.
DETAILS: Generate a "money out of range" error when the SUM aggregate function overflows on MONEY type columns, matching PostgreSQL's behavior. Restrict aggregation pushdown to DocDB for MONEY type columns only for MIN, MAX, and COUNT functions, which do not risk overflow. Perform addition with proper overflow checks in the PostgreSQL layer's cash_pl and cash_mi functions, now enhanced with added overflow verification to prevent silent overflow and incorrect sums.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#29955] DocDB: Fix memory leak in CompletedCallQueue when outbound call tracking is disabled
RELEASE NOTE: Eliminate memory leak by removing unused CompletedCallQueue when reactor_based_outbound_call_expiration_delay_ms is set to 0.
DETAILS: Prevent unbounded memory growth by disabling the allocation and queuing of CompletedCallEntry objects in the CompletedCallQueue when the flag reactor_based_outbound_call_expiration_delay_ms is set to 0. This flag disables stuck RPC tracking, which previously caused a memory leak by queuing outbound RPC calls without draining them. Removing the unused queue ensures stable memory consumption during RPC communication management on tserver and master processes.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#30979] CDC: Avoid scanning cdc_state twice in GetTabletIdsToPoll
RELEASE NOTE: Reduce latency by batching multiple tables in a single GetTabletListToPollForCDC RPC for CDC stream polling.
DETAILS: Batch multiple tables in one GetTabletListToPollForCDC RPC call to decrease latency during CDC stream initialization and refresh, especially for publications with many tables. Avoid redundant scans of the cdc_state table by materializing rows once per call and reusing them, cutting scan costs by half. This change optimizes polling efficiency when handling multiple tables without modifying existing behavior or checkpoint handling.

TITLE: [2024.2][#33533] docdb: Bump OpenSSL to 3.5.8
RELEASE NOTE: Update OpenSSL to version 3.5.8 to leverage the latest cryptographic improvements and fixes.
DETAILS: Upgrade OpenSSL to version 3.5.8 to incorporate the latest enhancements and bug fixes in cryptographic functions, which can lead to better security and performance for encrypted communications. This update helps maintain compliance with current security standards and ensures compatibility with newer protocols and features.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#30537] YSQL: Support ConnMgr runtime GFlag update & convert ysql_conn_mgr_log_settings to runtime
RELEASE NOTE: Support updating Connection Manager runtime flags with immediate config reload and SIGHUP signal.
DETAILS: Enable runtime updates for Connection Manager flags by introducing the kConnMgr tag and related DEFINE_*_CONN_MGR_*_FLAG macros that enforce naming conventions and trigger config reloads. Flags tagged kConnMgr are managed via the FlagUpdateCallback mechanism, which rewrites the Connection Manager config and sends a SIGHUP signal to reload settings immediately. This enhancement provides dynamic control over Connection Manager behavior, including log settings, without needing restarts, while ensuring thread-safe configuration reloads in the connection manager process.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32889] YSQL: Enable ConnMgr log_config by default
RELEASE NOTE: Log Connection Manager's config at startup by default via ysql_conn_mgr_log_settings for better incident debugging.
DETAILS: Log the Connection Manager's exact configuration options at startup by default using the ysql_conn_mgr_log_settings GFlag set to 'log_config'. This logging occurs at info level only once when Connection Manager starts, incurring minimal overhead. Capturing the config values at startup aids postmortem analysis by preserving the exact settings used, even though the on-disk config file is overwritten on updates. The GFlag retains backward compatibility by continuing to accept 'log_config' as a value without changing existing deployments' behavior.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33593] CDC: Fix walsender memory leak due to allocations on incorrent mem context
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent walsender memory leak by restoring proper memory context after aborting transactions when decoding records.
DETAILS: Ensure walsender allocations occur in the correct memory context by explicitly switching back from TopMemoryContext after aborting transactions in GetDynamicTypeEntity and YBCReadRecord. This fixes unbounded walsender memory growth caused when decoding records with fields of invalid type OIDs, such as user-defined types, by properly freeing memory during cached_records_context resets.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#31097] CDC: Skip adding unqualified tables to the VWAL
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent adding unqualified tables to VWAL polling list unless cdc_skip_unqualified_tables_for_polling flag is set.
DETAILS: Block adding expired or not-of-interest tables to the Virtual Write-Ahead Log (VWAL) polling list to avoid rendering replication slots unusable due to WAL or intents garbage collection errors. If such tables are added, an error is raised; however, setting the runtime flag cdc_skip_unqualified_tables_for_polling allows skipping these unqualified tables and continues polling with the qualified ones. This behavior applies to colocated tables with tablet active times behind expiry thresholds. Errors from VWAL in this context are not retryable and propagate to the client, ensuring users are explicitly aware of the table qualification status when managing VWAL polling.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#30145] docdb: Fixed use-after-free of TransactionCoordinator::Impl in ApplyingReplicated
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent process crashes by ensuring RPCs remain registered during transaction state callbacks until fully completed.
DETAILS: Avoid use-after-free crashes in transaction status handling by deferring RPC unregistration within TransactionCoordinator::Impl::ApplyingReplicated until callbacks finish. This change keeps RPCs registered in 'calls_' during callback execution and waits for completion before shutdown, covering all retry branches and preventing premature coordinator destruction. Added new test QLTransactionTest.StatusTabletDeletedDuringApplyingReplicated and a sync point to reliably reproduce and verify the fix, ensuring stable transaction status processing amidst tablet deletions and retries.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33606] DocDB: Limit clock-failure diagnostics to once per process
RELEASE NOTE: Limit clock fault diagnostics to a single thread to reduce CPU load and node unresponsiveness during failures.
DETAILS: Restrict the invocation of 'chronyc' diagnostics to only one thread when a clock fault is detected, preventing thousands of simultaneous calls that could spike system CPU and delay node shutdown. This change uses std::call_once to ensure diagnostics run once per process, causing other threads to wait for completion before aborting. The fix prevents prolonged unresponsiveness of the node that previously lasted minutes, allowing for quicker failure handling and minimizing throughput impact during clock skew events.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33471] DocDB: Keep LogReader alive for in-flight WAL reads across a concurrent Log::Close()
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent crashes by ensuring LogReader stays alive during concurrent WAL reads even if the tablet log closes mid-read.
DETAILS: Avoid segmentation faults by maintaining LogReader's lifecycle through shared ownership during ongoing WAL reads, even when the tablet's log is closed concurrently. The Log object holds its LogReader in a shared pointer, and GetLogReader returns a shared copy, allowing read operations to complete safely without premature destruction. Calls after Log::Close receive a retryable IllegalState error. This fix ensures stable read operations during tablet shutdown, deletion, or restart scenarios without delaying shutdown procedures.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33814] DocDB: Fix cluster balancer UI bug in counting tablets per table
RELEASE NOTE: Correct tablet counts per table on cluster balancer UI and reduce the load-distribution page load time.
DETAILS: Fix accurate tablet counting per table on the cluster balancer UI by adding the missing table filter, preventing inflated aggregated counts. Optimize the /load-distribution endpoint to lower computational complexity from O(num_tables * total_num_replicas) to O(total_num_replicas), which resolves potential timeout issues during UI page loading and enhances page responsiveness for better user experience.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32131] DocDB: Avoid flushing bootstrap state before txn loading finishes
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent data loss by ensuring correct transaction state flush only after all transactions finish loading during bootstrap.
DETAILS: Avoid flushing transaction bootstrap state prematurely before all transactions finish loading, which prevents incorrect min_replay_txn_first_write_ht values causing transactions to be skip-loaded on next bootstrap. This change ensures loader_.WaitAllLoaded is called during SimulateProcessRecentlyAppliedTransactions, maintaining accurate transaction state and avoiding silent data loss or fatal errors like 'Unexpected write id' during tablet bootstrap.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33648] DocDB: Check free disk space during RBS and writes
RELEASE NOTE: Check free disk space on both WAL and data disks continuously during remote bootstrap and writes to prevent overfilling.
DETAILS: Continuously monitor free disk space on both WAL and data disks during remote bootstrap and write operations to prevent starting or continuing these operations on nearly full disks. Introduce a DiskSpaceChecker that enforces thresholds defined by reject_writes_min_disk_space_pct and reject_writes_min_disk_space_mb flags. During remote bootstrap, check disk space before and between each SST file and WAL segment transfer to abort if disks are filling up. For writes, verify sufficient free space on both WAL and tablet data root directories to reject writes when either disk is low on space, preventing possible data or WAL disk exhaustion.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32524] YSQL: Guardrail yb_index_check() callers subject to row-level security
RELEASE NOTE: Enforce Row-Level Security (RLS) checks in yb_index_check to prevent unauthorized index validation on RLS-enabled tables.
DETAILS: Introduce a guardrail in yb_index_check to ensure users without RLS BYPASS permission cannot perform index validation on tables with RLS enabled. This change causes immediate execution abort with a clear error if the executing user lacks RLS bypass privileges, preventing incorrect or inconsistent results during index checks. Superusers retain full access. The implementation applies to 2024.2 branch without adding table locks or changing partitioned index behavior, maintaining backward compatibility while improving data access security during index validation.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33699] YSQL: Fix NULL crash in row comparison binds.
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent crashes during row comparisons involving NULL by correctly handling NULL bindings in key comparisons.
DETAILS: Enable safe execution of row comparison queries that include NULL values by leaving corresponding column values unbound and marking the need for recheck. Prevent backend crashes caused by passing null pointers for NULL key components in row comparisons, such as in queries like `(a,b)>(0,NULL)`. This approach maintains open bounds in document storage and ensures consistent behavior without fatal errors when handling NULL values in primary key comparisons with varlena columns.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32692] YSQL: fix DISTINCT pushdown over UNION ALL and partitioned tables
RELEASE NOTE: Enable DISTINCT pushdown to work correctly over UNION ALL and partitioned tables by fixing planner key mapping.
DETAILS: Allow DISTINCT pushdown into index scans for queries involving UNION ALL and partitioned tables by correcting how the planner maps Unique node keys to output columns. This fix addresses the issue where multiple tablets independently skip duplicates during index scanning but can still generate duplicate values across tablets. The planner now passes the scanned relation to make_unique_from_pathkeys, ensuring it properly recognizes child table equivalence classes and prevents planning failures like "could not find pathkey item to sort." This improves query planning accuracy for DISTINCT queries on UNION ALL and partitioned tables.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32261] DocDB: Reduce MetaCache lock contention on consensus info refresh
RELEASE NOTE: Reduce lock contention on tablet consensus info refresh to prevent client-wide dispatch stalls during leader changes.
DETAILS: Revamp tablet consensus info refresh to hold the global MetaCache mutex in shared mode for most operations, significantly reducing lock contention during leader change storms. This avoids client-wide dispatch stalls by letting multiple RPCs access cache data concurrently instead of serializing on an exclusive lock. The refresh process now uses up to three phases; the initial phase filters outdated or redundant consensus info under shared locks, minimizing exclusive lock usage. This change benefits both YSQL and YCQL by maintaining low latency and high availability during raft leadership churns, implemented with the enable_metacache_partial_refresh feature enabled by default.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#34162] YSQL: leave a stranded removing-permission index alone
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent deletion of YSQL indexes stranded at removing permissions to avoid missing DocDB tables while still referenced by Postgres.
DETAILS: Prevent deletion of YSQL indexes stuck at INDEX_PERM_INDEX_UNUSED state after removal attempts to protect DocDB tables still referenced by Postgres. By narrowing the YSQL update bucket to permissions below DO_BACKFILL, and skipping queuing of stranded indexes for deletion, this resolves failures where DML operations error with OBJECT_NOT_FOUND due to premature DocDB table removal. The change maintains safe transitions of YSQL index permissions and logs warnings for stranded indexes to ensure schema version reporting correctly clears states without deleting live data.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#30287] YSQL: Bypass RLS in yb_index_check row-count query
RELEASE NOTE: Bypass RLS policies for the row-count query in yb_index_check to ensure accurate index validation.
DETAILS: Ensure yb_index_check accurately verifies index consistency by bypassing Row-Level Security (RLS) policies on the row-count query. While scan checks always see all physical rows, the count query was previously affected by RLS, causing incorrect mismatch errors when the caller is subject to RLS policies. This change introduces the SECURITY_NOFORCE_RLS flag around the count query in get_expected_index_rowcount, so the row count reflects all rows, regardless of RLS, preventing false error reports and improving reliability during index validation.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#32859] YSQL: fix uninitialized ybgin amcostestimate outputs
RELEASE NOTE: Ensure ybgin cost estimates initialize all output parameters to prevent incorrect query plan selections.
DETAILS: Initialize all output parameters in ybgin's amcostestimate function to avoid using uninitialized values that cause incorrect cost calculations. This prevents the planner from erroneously choosing or rejecting ybgin index scans due to garbage values affecting selectivity, correlation, and pages estimates. As a result, query plans involving ybgin indexes become consistent between EXPLAIN output and execution, eliminating build-specific flakes and test failures. This fix aligns with cost estimation patterns used by pgvector extensions and disables unsupported queries correctly via the yb_test_ybgin_disable_cost_factor * disable_cost charge.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#29567] CDC: Do no check for response safe time correctness when it is not moved
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent logging incorrect DFATAL safe time violations when sending request's safe time without WAL data.
DETAILS: Avoid incorrect DFATAL logs of safe time violations during CDC streaming when no WAL records are sent due to 'wait_for_wal_update' or 'txn_load_in_progress' flags being true. This prevents confusion in logs by skipping the safe time correctness check if the response's safe time is just the request's safe time and not advanced beyond WAL record times. The change improves log accuracy without impacting data consistency or loss during CDC operations.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#34733] YSQL: stop matching yb_hash_code to every key column
RELEASE NOTE: Stop matching yb_hash_code to every index key column to prevent wrong query results and errors with IS NULL conditions.
DETAILS: Match yb_hash_code calls only to the specific hash key columns of an index, avoiding incorrect matches to range columns that caused wrong query results and join behavior. This prevents the planner from mistakenly removing needed LEFT JOINs and from marking join sides as unique incorrectly, which previously limited returned rows. It also fixes errors like 'NullTest indexqual has wrong key' for yb_hash_code IS [NOT] NULL conditions during index scans. New tests validate these corrections on versions 2025.2 and 2024.2.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#34839] DocDB: Fast backward scan can return wrong results or hang
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent fast backward scans from hanging or returning incorrect rows when using skip_prefix_locks and lower key bounds.
DETAILS: Avoid hangs or wrong results in fast backward scans with use_fast_backward_scan=true by properly checking regular entries against iterator bounds even after intent iterator exhaustion. This fixes cases where skip_prefix_locks is enabled, a tablet has a lower key bound (like a post-split child), and committed but unapplied rows cause lookup errors due to unchecked bound conditions. The fix ensures stable and correct backward scanning by correctly handling intent exhaustion and key bounds during iteration.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#28566] docdb: UUID comparison does not work for unknown UUID version as expected
RELEASE NOTE: Align UUID comparison to use raw version nibble to ensure consistent ordering between in-memory and on-disk data.
DETAILS: Use the raw version nibble for UUID comparisons in operator< to match DocDB's key encoding order, resolving discrepancies when handling UUID versions greater than 5. This change ensures that UUIDv7 sorts after UUIDv4, preventing missed rows during lookups and filters involving mixed UUID versions. The ordering now matches Cassandra's uuid sorting logic, enabling correct SELECT queries with IN conditions across different UUID versions.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#34756] YSQL: Avoid applying oversized fields in conn mgr
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent connection manager crashes by ignoring startup parameters exceeding 128 bytes to avoid memory overruns.
DETAILS: Protect connection manager stability by restricting processing of startup parameters larger than 128 bytes, such as .application_name or yb_ycm_internal_client_cert, preventing heap overruns that corrupt OpenSSL state and cause pre-authentication crashes. Fields exceeding this length are silently ignored, eliminating remote crash or denial-of-service risks triggered by unauthenticated clients sending oversized values in startup messages.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#34841] DocDB: ByteBuffer::EnsureCapacity loops forever on oversized requests
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent infinite loop & high CPU in ByteBuffer::EnsureCapacity by handling oversized requests and allocation failures.
DETAILS: Replace the previous infinite loop in ByteBuffer::EnsureCapacity that occurred on extremely large capacity requests causing CPU to spin at 100% by computing the required capacity directly. When a requested capacity is too large to fit in size_t after doubling, use the requested capacity as is instead of looping endlessly. Also add explicit checks for malloc failures to abort with a fatal error reporting the requested capacity, preventing crashes later from null buffer usage. This ensures robust handling of large buffer growth requests and predictable failure behavior on allocation limits without affecting normal capacity growth performance.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#34947,#35147] DocDB: Fast backward scan can miss intents after a forward seek
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent backward scans from missing rows or returning stale data by fixing iterator positioning during multi-version column reads.
DETAILS: Avoid missing or outdated rows in fast backward scans by ensuring intent and regular iterators are valid before seeking backward. This resolves issues where committed but not yet applied transactions or the reading transaction's own writes could be partially invisible, especially on colocated and hash-sharded tables and indexes with DESC primary keys. The fix updates SeekBeforeSubKey to properly prepare iterators using SeekToLast or a newly introduced IntentSeekBeforeKey, preventing skipped intents and stale reads. This correction enhances read consistency, especially when max_prevs_to_avoid_seek is zero, and is covered by regression tests.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#35544] CDC: Fix incorrect intent barrier movement during successive stream creation
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent intent data from being prematurely deleted by aligning intent retention barriers across concurrent replication streams.
DETAILS: Align intent retention barriers between transaction participants and tablet metadata to prevent premature deletion of intents when multiple CDC streams are created sequentially. This fixes issues where a new CDC stream could advance the transaction participant's intent barrier beyond the strictest barrier set by earlier streams, leading to 'GCed intents' errors during streaming. The fix ensures consistent retention barriers to maintain integrity of in-progress transactions across all replication slots, improving stability for concurrent logical replication setups.

TITLE: [2024.2][#28566] Revert: DocDB: UUID comparison does not work for unknown UUID version as expected
RELEASE NOTE: Restore UUID comparison behavior to ensure consistent query results for mixed-version UUIDs in YCQL.
DETAILS: Correct UUID comparison to align in-memory ordering with on-disk key encoding for mixed UUID versions, preventing query misses and duplicates when filtering by frozen sets or maps containing UUIDs of versions greater than 5. This fix avoids inconsistent results in YCQL queries that use UUIDs with unknown versions, ensuring rows inserted before and after upgrades remain accessible and identifiable when queried with predicates like IN on UUID collections.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#33143] CDC: Resolving schema packings using mapping from tablet_metadata
RELEASE NOTE: Resolve CDC stalls after node restarts by mapping schema packings from tablet metadata to handle version mismatches.
DETAILS: Prevent CDC replication from stalling after node restarts by accurately resolving schema packing versions from tablet metadata. This avoids errors like 'Schema packing not found' during CDC resume attempts when schema changes occur close to the time of row writes. The fix maps the correct schema used at row write time, ensuring smooth replication progress even after restarts, thereby eliminating permanent replication stalls caused by schema version mismatches. This change benefits CDC users running long stress tests or dynamic schema operations, improving reliability without requiring manual cache resets.

TITLE: [DocDB] `MemTrackerTest.TcMallocRootTracker` fails on release branches: Expected equality of these values:...
RELEASE NOTE: Address intermittent failures in MemTrackerTest.TcMallocRootTracker on release branches to stabilize test results.
DETAILS: Resolve instability in the MemTrackerTest.TcMallocRootTracker test which has been failing intermittently at a high rate on release branches, notably branch 2026.1, while remaining stable on master. The failure, marked by test assertion errors in C++, is affecting continuous integration reliability and occurs predominantly on the alma8-gcc15-fastdebug lane. This fix aims to reduce the failure rate back to historical levels, improving test consistency and confidence in release builds.

TITLE: [YSQL] Make yb_insert_on_conflict_read_batch_size user-settable
RELEASE NOTE: Allow all users to set yb_insert_on_conflict_read_batch_size, enabling session-level control of insert conflict read batching.
DETAILS: Permit any user to set yb_insert_on_conflict_read_batch_size, previously restricted to superusers, allowing individual sessions to enable or disable insert conflict read batching. This change facilitates applying workarounds for batching bugs or performance tuning without operator or superuser intervention. Note that cluster-level defaults set via ysql_pg_conf_csv or by role/database remain as defaults but can be overridden per session. Operators lose the ability to enforce cluster-wide batching settings, so careful coordination is advised. This adjustment paves the way for broader stability improvements and user-specific optimization.

TITLE: [YSQL] INSERT ON CONFLICT batching writes past its slot arrays when yb_insert_on_conflict_read_batch_size changes during the statement
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent out-of-bounds errors by ensuring INSERT ON CONFLICT batching uses consistent read batch sizes during a statement.
DETAILS: Maintain internal slot array sizes for INSERT ON CONFLICT batching based on the initial yb_insert_on_conflict_read_batch_size setting to prevent out-of-bounds memory access when this setting changes mid-statement. This avoids runtime errors and crashes caused by dynamically changing batch sizes during buffered writes, especially when expressions or set_config alter the parameter within the statement. This stabilizes behavior and safeguards against data corruption or process termination during bulk inserts with conflict handling.

TITLE: [YSQL] Index scan returns wrong rows when a non-equality ANY condition shares a key column with another condition, [YSQL] Non-equality ANY on a hash column becomes an index condition, which can crash the backend or return wrong rows
RELEASE NOTE: Return correct rows for index scans involving non-equality ANY conditions sharing key columns by properly setting needs_recheck.
DETAILS: Ensure index scans correctly handle non-equality ANY conditions on key columns by preventing these array keys from being misinterpreted as scalar values during binding. This change sets needs_recheck to true for such conditions regardless of other qualifiers to avoid incorrect results. It also prevents non-equality ANY conditions on hash columns from becoming index conditions, eliminating backend crashes and wrong rows. The behavior controlled by the flag yb_enable_advanced_index_cond_fold is refined to maintain accuracy for equality and range cases involving ANY conditions on index or hash columns.

TITLE: [Build] Script to remove old thirdparty versions from /opt/yb-build/thirdparty
RELEASE NOTE: Add a script to remove outdated thirdparty versions from /opt/yb-build/thirdparty to save disk space.
DETAILS: Introduce a script located in build-support to automatically delete outdated versions of thirdparty dependencies from /opt/yb-build/thirdparty, retaining only the newest version for each release and kind. This prevents the directory from growing excessively large over time due to accumulated old versions. The script runs in dry-run mode by default to allow safe inspection before actual deletion, helping developers manage disk usage effectively without manual cleanup.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#37494] YSQL: Escape identifiers in auto-analyze ANALYZE statements
RELEASE NOTE: Escape double quotes properly in schema and table names for auto-analyze to prevent syntax errors and retries.
DETAILS: Ensure the auto-analyze service correctly escapes double quotes in schema and table identifiers by using pgwrapper::PqEscapeIdentifier. This prevents syntax errors during ANALYZE commands on tables or schemas with embedded double quotes like "s""chema"."t""bl". Consequently, the auto-analyze process completes successfully without indefinite retries, maintaining accurate and timely statistics collection for query optimization.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#37381] CDC: Ignore aborted subtransactions when populating intra-transaction before image
RELEASE NOTE: Ignore aborted subtransactions when populating intra-transaction before images to ensure correct CDC data consistency.
DETAILS: Populate the intra-transaction before image by accounting for aborted subtransaction IDs within the TransactionOperationContext. This prevents visibility of rolled-back writes to the before image, ensuring that only committed changes are streamed. The aborted subtransaction set from the APPLY record is now passed through ProcessIntents to PopulateCDCSDKIntentRecord, removing incorrect before images caused by savepoint rollbacks. This update targets correctness in change data capture streams when cdc_enable_intra_transactional_before_image is enabled.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#37481] CDC: Fix data loss when resuming a partially streamed transaction
RELEASE NOTE: Prevent data loss when resuming CDC streams by correctly handling partial transactions spanning multiple GetChanges calls.
DETAILS: Ensure that resuming CDC streams for transactions with more intents than cdc_max_stream_intent_records correctly processes WAL records in commit order. When a partial transaction is split across multiple GetChanges calls, the next call properly waits for sorted WAL updates and avoids mixing intents from different transactions. This prevents streaming rows with incorrect commit times and avoids prematurely acknowledging unrelated APPLY records, eliminating data loss during CDC resumption.

TITLE: [BACKPORT 2024.2][#36725] CDC: Convert QLValue to Datum with correct catalog snapshot
RELEASE NOTE: Stream changes reliably after adding an extension-type column without slot failure or restart.
DETAILS: Ensure logical replication slots continue streaming changes seamlessly after adding columns of extension types (like hstore, halfvec, sparsevec) via ALTER TABLE, preventing failures due to 'cache lookup failed for type 0'. Avoid interruption or slot dropping, enabling consistent replication across supported extension types and various cluster setups for ongoing insert streaming without manual intervention.
